4	
5	# The stored image is the contract
6	
7	> **Scope amended by
8	> [ADR-0007](0007-fit-to-width-and-a-vector-zoom-ceiling.md).** Everything below
9	> is about _raster_ receipts. 100% is now fit-to-_width_, and an emailed receipt
10	> — an SVG — has no pixel ceiling to stop at.
11	
12	## Context & decision
13	
14	`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
15	_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
16	resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.
17	
18	The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
19	artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
20	the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
21	a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
22	judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:
23	
24	- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
25	  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
26	- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
27	  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
28	  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
29	- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
30	  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
31	  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
32	  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
33	  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
34	- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
35	  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
36	  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
37	  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
38	  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.
39	
40	## Considered options
41	
42	- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
43	  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
44	  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
45	- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
46	  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
47	  anyway."
48	- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
49	  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
50	  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
51	  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
52	- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
53	  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
54	  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
55	- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
56	  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
57	  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
58	  screen is a real pixel.
59	
60	## Consequences
61	
62	- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
63	  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
64	  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
65	- **A PNG screenshot can come out _larger_ than it arrived.** JPEG spends bits on
66	  the hard edges of rendered text that PNG encodes almost for free, so for a
67	  sharp-edged e-receipt screenshot already within the pixel budget the transcode
68	  can grow the file. Measured, not theoretical. This is the cost of the single
69	  stored format and is accepted; the keep-the-smaller-file guard above is the
70	  alternative if it ever matters. Photographs — the overwhelming majority —
71	  shrink by well over half.
72	- **JPEG has no alpha, so the canvas must be painted white first.** A
73	  transparent-background PNG composites onto _black_ by default (the HTML spec
74	  requires it), which would store dark text on a black field as the only copy of
75	  the receipt.
76	- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
77	  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
78	  deliberately over faking magnification.
79	- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
80	  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
81	  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
82	  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
83	- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
84	  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
85	  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
86	  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
87	  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
88	  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
89	- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
90	  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
91	  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

All three slices are in and the gate is green. Summary:

## A — the renderer
- **`supabase/functions/_shared/textRender.ts`** (new): `stripHtml`, `layoutText`, `renderTextToSvg`, `renderTextToSvgBytes`. 1100px @ 14px monospace, `WRAP_COLUMNS` computed (126) from the geometry, character-breaking for unbreakable tokens, blank-run collapse, `data-yfl-render-version="2"` marker. 22 tests in `textRender.test.ts`.
- **`textToImage` deleted** from `mistral.ts` *and* from `OcrPort` — it was a port method wired in `index.ts` and stubbed in `handler.test.ts`, not a bare import. The handler now calls the pure function directly and keeps `emailBodyText` raw for Mistral alongside a stripped `emailRenderText`.

## B — the viewer
- `calculateFitDimensions` is width-only; `VECTOR_MAX_ZOOM = 800`; `VIEWPORT_FRACTION` → scalar `VIEWPORT_WIDTH_FRACTION` with the vertical bound now a `max-h-[80vh]` class (your Q3 — yes, it was doing nothing computational once width binds).
- Wheel is `ctrlKey`/`metaKey`-gated and continuous (`exp(-delta × 0.005)`), with a `deltaMode === 1` normalisation for Firefox.
- `pdfDetection.ts` → **`receiptFileType.ts`** with `isVectorFile`; modal passes `isVector`; vector thumbnails crop `object-top object-cover`; `object-top` added to both list pages.

## C — the backfill
`scripts/backfillEmailReceiptSvgs.ts` + `npm run backfill:email-svgs` (`op run --env-file=.env -- tsx …`). Dry-run by default, `--apply` to write, overwrites in place, no DB writes, imports the real renderer, skips anything already at version 2. **I have not run it** — not even the dry run, since it consumes the `.env` FIFO and reads production. Your call when.

I resolved the design's open question: recovered text goes through the stripper only when it sniffs as HTML, and the dry run prints which files that fired on.

## D — docs
ADR 0007 (+ scope banner on 0006), domain model (`Emailed Text Receipt` term, both amended invariants), five backlog entries, CLAUDE.md pattern, design doc marked built with four deviations recorded, `git mv`'d to `plans-done/`.

**Gate:** `check` 0/0, `check:deno` clean, `lint` clean, 1403 server tests + 138 browser tests pass. Nothing staged, nothing committed.

Two things to flag:
- I couldn't verify `.env` actually contains `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (FIFO — reading it would consume it). The script fails loudly by name if it's missing.
- Beyond the design: `xml:space="preserve"` is now set, because the old SVG was silently collapsing indentation and column alignment in plain-text receipts. That's why the `<tspan>`s are joined with no separator.

> response body. A run of `401 Invalid webhook signature` there means the Supabase

### Inbound Webhook Rejected (401 / 500)

The webhook **fails closed** on signature verification (`resend/index.ts`): a bad
signature returns `401`, a missing `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` returns `500`, and the
event is not processed.

1. Open <https://resend.com/webhooks> → your endpoint → copy the **Signing Secret**.
2. Set it in Supabase so the two match exactly:
   `supabase secrets set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET='whsec_…'`
3. Redeploy: `supabase functions deploy resend`. Do not disable verification to
   "unblock" ingestion — that lets any caller inject receipts into any account.

### Emails Not Sending

1. Check `RESEND_API_KEY` is set in Supabase secrets
2. Verify domain is verified in Resend dashboard
3. Check function logs for error messages

   "unblock" ingestion — that lets any caller inject receipts into any account.

Both answered, and the second one is a "no":

## 1. Deploying the function

There's no automation for this — Vercel builds the SvelteKit app only, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` deploys nothing. Edge functions are a manual CLI step:

```bash
supabase functions deploy resend
```

The project is already linked (`acepytsyfbfhbwraswqj`), and `verify_jwt = false` is declared in *both* `supabase/config.toml` `[functions.resend]` and `supabase/functions/resend/deno.json`, so you don't need `--no-verify-jwt` — the webhook won't start rejecting Resend with 401. The CLI bundles the whole import graph from `index.ts`, so `_shared/textRender.ts` goes with it; the `.test.ts` files don't, since nothing imports them.

**Running it locally isn't really a thing here**, and that's pre-existing — `docs/local-dev.md` says so. `supabase functions serve resend` works against the local stack, but the webhook is inbound-only and fails closed on the svix signature, so exercising it means a tunnel plus a real Resend delivery.

For *this* change you don't need any of that. The renderer is a pure function with 22 node tests, and you can just look at its output:

```bash
open /tmp/yfl-sample-receipt.svg
```

I already generated one from a realistic forwarded body: **1100 × 300px, 13 lines**. The same input under the old renderer was 800 × 360px with the tracking URL clipped at ~90 characters — so it's both shorter (blank runs collapsed) and complete (URL wrapped onto two lines).

## 2. No — the backfill doesn't need the deploy

They're independent. `scripts/backfillEmailReceiptSvgs.ts` runs under `tsx` on your machine and imports `textRender.ts` from disk; it talks to Postgres and Storage directly with the service-role key and never calls the edge function.

**But deploy first anyway**, for consistency: any receipt that arrives by email between the backfill and the deploy gets rendered by the old 800px code. Not fatal — those land at version 0 and a second `--apply` run would pick them up — but it's avoidable by ordering it:

```bash
supabase functions deploy resend
npm run backfill:email-svgs              # dry run — read the output
npm run backfill:email-svgs -- --apply
```

One caveat on the middle step: it goes through `op run --env-file=.env`, which consumes the `.env` FIFO. Don't have `npm run dev` running at the same time, and expect to need a fresh shell between the dry run and the apply.
Rip out the backfill code, it's been run once, committed and now can be dropped.

lines: - **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.

- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.

- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work. **Extended 2026-08-03:** the wheel path is now modifier-gated and continuous, so also confirm that a plain mouse wheel and a two-finger trackpad scroll _scroll_, that trackpad pinch zooms smoothly rather than in 50% lurches, and that Ctrl/Cmd + wheel zooms toward the cursor.

-- **Delete `scripts/backfillEmailReceiptSvgs.ts` once it has been run.** One-shot, local-only, `--apply`-gated re-render of existing `.svg` receipts against the current renderer. It is throwaway by design and its version marker makes a second run a no-op, but leaving it in the tree leaves a service-role storage-overwrite script lying around.

- **An emailed receipt's SVG height is unbounded.** `renderTextToSvg` emits `lines × 20 + 40` px with no cap, and wrapping only ever _increases_ the line count. A pathological forwarded thread could produce a document tall enough that browsers refuse to rasterize it. No cap was added deliberately — the whole point of the change was to stop losing content — so the fix, if it is ever needed, is pagination or a "… N further lines" marker, not silent truncation.

- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. The middle one is a query run purely to log its result — it is labelled "for debugging" and nothing consumes it. A fourth logs every created receipt in `insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` (`:347`); it is the only remaining reader of `family_id` on `InsertedReceiptRow`, so deleting it may let that type collapse back to `ReceiptRow`. Delete the logs and the debug query.

- **Receipts page fetches every family expense just to colour one column.** `loadCategories` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:254`) calls `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — a full paged pass over `receipts` with an embed — solely to build `categoryMap`. Now that the [Category column](plans-done/2026-08-03-classify-on-receipts-page-design.md) has shipped, that second full-table read sits on the render path — on a page that has already loaded every receipt once — rather than only behind the edit modal. It should read `expense_categories` for the receipts already in hand instead.

lines: - **Adding a column to `receipts` means editing three hand-maintained lists, and the compiler checks none of them.** They are `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (an allow-list — a field missing from it is silently stripped from every `update()`, no error, the value just never saves), `buildReceiptPatch` in `src/lib/utils/receiptPatch.ts` (what the edit modal actually sends, shared by the Receipts, Reconciliation and Expenses pages), and the `isDirty` comparison in `ReceiptEditModal.svelte` (miss it and closing the modal discards an unsaved edit **with no prompt**). It used to be five — the three pages each hand-wrote their own patch literal and had already drifted from one another. Do not reintroduce a per-page patch object. Two related rules: **`buildReceiptPatch` carries only what the modal can edit**, because writing back a field the modal merely read turns any save into a lost update; and **`suspicious_date` belongs to `ReceiptService.update` alone**, which forces it to `false` whenever `transaction_date` is present — a page-level copy of that rule is dead code, which is exactly what the old Receipts literal was, under a comment claiming the opposite.

- **A Note's empty value is `NULL`, never `''`.** `normalizeNote` (`src/lib/utils/receiptPatch.ts`) is the single gate; a textarea hands back `''` when cleared and `'  '` after a stray space, and letting either through would give "no note" three spellings that every reader — preview, dirty check, a future export — would have to know. The 1024 limit is enforced by the `receipts_notes_length` CHECK constraint; the client check is UX only, and deliberately has **no `maxlength`** so an over-long paste arrives whole and its author chooses what to cut rather than having the browser silently truncate it. JS `.length` over-counts astral characters relative to Postgres `char_length`, which is safe in that direction only.

- **Auto-categorization is applied by the database, not the client.** The `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` trigger on `receipts` assigns the family's vendor-rule category (`source='auto'`, only when no `expense_categories` row exists). **Do not reintroduce client-side assignment** — `ReceiptService.autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` was deleted precisely because it only ever covered browser upload, leaving manual entry, splits, the historical importer, and email ingestion uncategorized. The trigger is best-effort by design (it swallows its own errors) so a categorization failure can never abort receipt creation. `applyAllVendorRules` still runs on Expenses **and** Receipts page load, but only as a retroactive net: a rule created after a receipt exists fans out solely over the rows that were on screen at the time. Related trap: **SQL `normalize_vendor()` must match `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` exactly** — `vendor_pattern` is stored already-normalized, so drift raises no error and rules just silently stop matching. Both are pinned to the shared list in `src/lib/utils/vendorNormalizationCases.ts`; the SQL half is only checked by `npm run test:integration`, which needs a live stack and gates nothing. Normalization is lowercase → trim → strip non-alphanumerics → collapse whitespace, and that order is load-bearing (trimming last would change the result).

-- **An email with no usable attachment becomes an SVG we typeset ourselves.** `renderTextToSvg` (`supabase/functions/_shared/textRender.ts`) wraps and lays out the body; the handler uploads it as `image/svg+xml`. Three things follow. **The wrapping must happen in Deno** — an SVG loaded through `` renders in restricted mode, where `` HTML is not rendered, so the browser cannot be asked to break lines. **`stripHtml` applies to the picture only** — the raw body still goes to Mistral, because there is no regression corpus to prove that changing what the model sees does not make extraction worse. And **`textRender.ts` is checked by both checkers** (`deno check` for the directory, `tsc` because `scripts/` imports it), so no `Deno` globals and explicit `.ts` specifiers. Zoom for these is governed by [ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-fit-to-width-and-a-vector-zoom-ceiling.md), not 0006: a vector has no pixel grid, so the 1:1 ceiling is a category error and it gets a flat 800% instead.

content.text:
Done. Gate green — 1403 tests, `check` / `check:deno` / `lint` all clean.

Removed:
- `scripts/backfillEmailReceiptSvgs.ts` (via `git rm`, staged as deleted)
- the `backfill:email-svgs` npm script
- the backlog item asking for its deletion

Three docs asserted things that the deletion made false, so I corrected them rather than leaving them to rot:

- **`textRender.ts` header** claimed "checked by both `deno check` and `tsc`". That was only true because `scripts/` imported it — with the script gone, `tsc` no longer reaches the file and `check:deno` is its only checker. Same claim removed from the CLAUDE.md bullet.
- **`RENDER_VERSION`'s comment** described itself as something "the backfill" reads. The marker is worth keeping — it's stamped on every stored SVG and is how a future re-render would know which generation produced what — so I kept it and reworded it to say that instead.
- **The design doc's status line** said the backfill "has not been run yet". Now records that it ran once and the script was deleted as designed.

`scripts/` is back to just `demo/`.

One thing worth knowing: the `.ts` import specifiers and the absence of `Deno` globals in `textRender.ts` are now enforced by only one checker each rather than both. The explicit `.ts` extensions are still required (Deno won't infer them); the "no `Deno` globals" rule is no longer checked by anything, since nothing outside the Deno directory imports the module. It's still true today, and it's the constraint that would need re-checking if something under `src/` or `scripts/` ever imports it again.
